acceptance_criteria: Positive: a single writer appends, flushes at the documented boundaries and finalizes by atomic replacement, leaving the stream and manifest internally consistent.

Negative: a second concurrent or repeated writer for the same run, an interrupted finalization, or a truncated last JSONL record is detected and reported as failed or incomplete; reopening the damaged run leaves every original byte unchanged.
No power-loss durability is claimed beyond the explicitly documented and verified filesystem contract; the claim is a bounded local guarantee, not a distributed or hardware guarantee.
applicability: Phase 2 Argus Lite bounded software allocation (bounded run evidence persistence, X-COM observation projection import and read-only reconstruction). status 'accepted' records internal engineering intent only; it is not implementation satisfaction, runtime evidence, scientific validity, or external delivery acceptance.
statement: Argus shall enforce exactly one owning writer per run and a writer state machine (new to open to closed, or open to failed), reject reuse or overwrite of an existing run, and document its flush/fsync/rename boundaries and partial-write handling; recovery shall reopen only bounded prefixes and report incomplete or damaged evidence without rewriting, upgrading or mutating the original evidence files.
title: Single-writer state, documented durability and non-mutating recovery
verification_intent: Planned to be exercised through the ARGUS2-UNIT, ARGUS2-STATIC, ARGUS2-INTEGRATION and ARGUS2-VALIDATION measures defined in the ARGUS2 verification-design stage, including the real accepted XDL compiler output, the owned C++ X-COM observation-record producer fixture, the offline built-and-installed wheel and the read-only reader. No runtime, live, availability, compatibility, parity or readiness claim is made.
